newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks off on trade gap speculation-traders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks off on trade gap speculation-traders.

text.p: Brazilian shares dropped 1.81 percent on speculation over a larger-than-expected trade deficit for July after figures were leaked to the market, brokers said.
"This is just speculation. People are over-reacting to the trade balance," a local trader said.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 most-traded shares dropped 233 points to 12,639 points on volume totalling 103.5 million reais ($95.6 million).

Brokers said the market declined on fears of a wider-than-expected trade gap, citing a possible July deficit ranging from $600 million to $800 million. The figures could not be independently confirmed. Economists were expecting an average gap of about $570 million for the month, according to the latest Reuters survey BRAAL.

Folha de S. Paulo newspaper reported Friday the trade gap for the July 1 through July 30 period reached $610 million. Traders said they had heard the gap for the last day of the month was about $200 million, mostly due to the purchase of two planes.

Brokers also said the market fell back due to rises in U.S. interest rates and slightly worse-than-expected first half earnings for Telebras, whose preferred is the local benchmark issue accounting for 60 percent of daily trade.
Telebras preferred fell 2.48 percent to 157.01 reais by 1110 local/1010 EDT in Sao Paulo.

Brokers said Telebras's consolidated net profit of 1.5 billion reais in the January-June period was a little low if the firm was to meet forecasts for a year-end profit of more than 4.0 billion reais.
